version.changelog: Automated publish from OutlitAI/outlit-agent-skills@e4108f583f0a82322b8d9fc9a83667526ac15c8d after merged skill changes.

llm.summary: This is a coherent Outlit customer-intelligence skill with disclosed sensitive data access and a less-safe remote shell install option users should handle carefully.

dimensions.detail: Use of OUTLIT_API_KEY, OAuth/MCP, third-party integration credentials, and customer/business data is sensitive but proportionate to the customer-intelligence purpose and is described in the artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses npm and Homebrew install metadata, but also presents a fast `curl ... | bash` installer that executes remote shell code without pinned integrity verification.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions include useful limits: use high-level tools first, request only needed fields, cite evidence, keep SQL read-only, and only change customer ownership or access when explicitly asked.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The artifact itself is markdown and has no executable payload, but setup may install the Outlit CLI, modify agent skill configuration, and persist credentials or local CLI state through normal Outlit authentication flows.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The skill’s capabilities match its stated purpose: querying Outlit customer profiles, timelines, facts, source evidence, search results, revenue, churn, and read-only SQL analytics.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install only if you intend to let agents query Outlit-connected customer and revenue data. Prefer the npm or Homebrew install path over the remote shell shortcut, review any integration credential setup before submitting secrets, and allow ownership or access changes only when you explicitly request them.
llm.findings: [SQP-2] expected: The remote shell installer is an installation convenience for the CLI and is purpose-aligned, but users should prefer npm/Homebrew or inspect and verify the installer before running it.
